title: Indulgent God, Whose Bounteous Care
description: Indulgent God, Whose Bounteous Care in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 947 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Evening Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In-dul-gent God, whose boun-teous care O'er all thy works is shown, O let my grate-ful praise and prayer As-cend be-fore thy throne!

lines: O'er all thy works is shown,
O let my grateful praise and prayer
What mercies has this day bestowed!
Now may sweet slumbers close my eyes,
And let my waking thoughts arise
So bless each future day and night,
Till life's fond scene is o'er;
At length, to realms of endless light
